raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

In a dense MLP whose down projection is a compressed-tensors W4A4 NVFP4 linear, `silu_and_mul` writes a BF16
activation that `fp4_quantize` immediately reads back. This PR uses FlashInfer's activation+quantization fused kernel  `flashinfer.quantization.silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quantize` for this scenario, plus a fix for 3-D inputs to the NVFP4 linear.

## Modifications

- `SiluAndMul.fuse_output_quant(down_proj)` registers the consumer once at build time: only W4A4 NVFP4 linears, only
  on NVIDIA GPUs (`is_cuda()`), and only when FlashInfer's kernel and CuTe-DSL are available. `forward_cuda` keeps the
  unfused path first and uses it for other dtypes, widths not divisible by 32, non-contiguous inputs, LoRA and sequence
  parallelism. There is no batch-size threshold: see the speed tests below.
- `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4.apply_weights` accepts the pre-quantized `(fp4, block_scale, dtype, leading_dims)` input
  or a plain activation, and inputs with leading dims (`[batch, seq, hidden]`, as vision towers pass): flattened for the
  quant and GEMM, output restored to the leading dims. Before, `mm_fp4` rejected 3-D inputs.
- Wired into `LlamaMLP` and `Qwen2MLP`. The existing block-FP8 decode fusion (`DenseSiluAndMulQuant`) is unaffected. On by default where it applies.
- Tests: `test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant.py` (SM100+: the kernel's output vs
`silu_and_mul` + `fp4_quantize`, codes and swizzled scales, 1 to 4100 tokens, leading dims),
`test/registered/unit/layers/test_silu_and_mul_nvfp4_fusion.py` (CPU: which linears are fused, fallbacks, non-NVIDIA
and no-FlashInfer cases), and a manual benchmark `test/manual/kernels/bench_silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant.py` (CUDA graph,
several seeds)

## Accuracy Tests

- Kernel: 0 byte mismatches vs `silu_and_mul` + `fp4_quantize` (FP4 codes and swizzled block scales) at every
  benchmarked shape (1 to 32768 tokens, three widths, several seeds) on RTX 5090
- RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4, GSM8K 5-shot, all 1319 questions, RTX 5090: main (f2d3188) 0.682, this PR: 0.688

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End to end, RedHatAI/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4 on an RTX 5090, `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random-ids --random-range-ratio 1`, three seeds per side, main (f2d3188) then PR on the same GPU:

| workload | % Perf change (median) |
|---|---|
| prefill: 1024 prompts x 2048 tokens, 1 output token, 64 in flight (input tok/s) |  +4.0% |
| decode: 512 prompts x 256 tokens, 512 output tokens, 128 in flight (output tok/s) | +0.2% |

Kernel (`test/manual/kernels/bench_silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant.py`, CUDA graph, 5 seeds), fused vs `silu_and_mul` +`fp4_quantize`, lowest speedup over the three down_proj widths (14336 Llama-3.1-8B, 12288 Qwen3-8B, 8192 Llama-3.2-3B):

| GPU | 64 | 128 | 256 | 512 | 2048 | 8192 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 5090 | 0.96x | 0.98x | 1.28x | 1.41x | 1.43x | 1.83x |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
[by Claude Code] This review is done by agents. Please feel free to disagree if they do not make sense.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`_accepts_nvfp4_input` uses `getattr(linear, "scheme", None)` and `getattr(scheme, "accepts_prequantized_input", False)`. SGLang does not allow defensive `getattr`. `LinearBase` already defines `scheme = None` for exactly this `is None` check. If the flag is renamed later, this code silently turns the fusion off instead of failing.

**Fix**

Type the argument as `LinearBase` and read the field directly: `isinstance(linear.scheme, CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4)` with a local import. Or declare `accepts_prequantized_input: bool = False` on `BaseLinearScheme` and check `linear.scheme is not None and linear.scheme.accepts_prequantized_input`. The CPU test's `_linear()` helper then needs a real `scheme` field.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

This adds a second way for an NVFP4 linear to take a pre-quantized input. `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.apply` already accepts an `(fp4, scale)` tuple when `layer._accepts_prequantized_fp4` is set (used by `qwen3_5.py` and `deepseek_v2.py`). This PR adds a scheme flag and a different 4-tuple, `(fp4, scale, dtype, leading_dims)`, for compressed-tensors only. So `SiluAndMul.fuse_output_quant` never fuses ModelOpt NVFP4 Llama/Qwen2/Qwen3 checkpoints, although their `down_proj` can already take a quantized input.

**Fix**

Use one opt-in and one tuple layout for both NVFP4 linear methods, and let `fuse_output_quant` accept ModelOpt W4A4 linears too. If ModelOpt is out of scope for this PR, say so in the description.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

No test calls `CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4.apply_weights` with the new inputs. `test_silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant.py` checks only the activation kernel, and `test_silu_and_mul_nvfp4_fusion.py` checks only the gating. Nothing checks that a 3-D input now returns `[batch, seq, N]` (the fix this PR claims), or that the 4-tuple skips `fp4_quantize` and restores `leading_dims`.

**Fix**

Add a CPU case to `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_compressed_tensors_fp4_schemes.py`. Patch `fp4_quantize` and `fp4_gemm` in this module with shape-only fakes, then call `apply_weights` with a 3-D tensor and with a 4-tuple. Assert the output shapes, and assert that `fp4_quantize` is not called for the tuple.

+"""SiluAndMul fused with the NVFP4 activation quant of the next linear (FlashInfer's kernel)
+gives the same FP4 codes and block scales as silu_and_mul followed by fp4_quantize."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.activation import SiluAndMul, silu_and_mul
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.schemes import (
+    CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4,
+)
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp4_utils import fp4_quantize
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, enter_scope, published_topology
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+
+def _sf_offsets(rows: int, groups: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Offsets of the [rows, groups] block scales in the 128x4 swizzled layout."""
+    k_tiles = (groups + 3) // 4
+    m = torch.arange(rows).unsqueeze(1)
+    k = torch.arange(groups).unsqueeze(0)
+    return (
+        (m // 128) * k_tiles * 512
+        + (k // 4) * 512
+        + (m % 32) * 16
+        + ((m % 128) // 32) * 4
+        + (k % 4)
+    ).cuda()
+
+
+@unittest.skipIf(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] < 10,
+    "NVFP4 activation quantization requires SM100+",
+)

+
+    def _fused_act(self, global_scale):

+        )

+"""SiLU-and-mul followed by NVFP4 activation quantization: silu_and_mul + fp4_quantize vs
+FlashInfer's fused kernel (used by SiluAndMul.fuse_output_quant), at the down-projection widths
+of common dense models.
+
+Requires SM100+ (NVFP4). Each (model, tokens) point is timed once per seed (fresh random input
+and global scale) inside a CUDA graph (triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph, kernel time only);
+"--modes eager graph" also times eager calls, which include the host launch cost. The table shows
+the mean and standard deviation over seeds. The fused output is checked against the unfused one
+first (packed FP4 bytes, <= 2e-3 mismatch: the FP32 SiLU may round to a neighbouring BF16 value
+now and then).
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+
+import torch
+import triton
+
+# Down-projection input widths (intermediate sizes).
+MODELS = {
+    "Llama-3.1-8B": 14336,
+    "Qwen3-8B": 12288,
+    "Llama-3.2-3B": 8192,
+}
+TOKENS = [1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 96, 128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 1024, 2048, 8192, 32768]
+
+
+def unfused(x, global_scale):
+    from sglang.srt.layers.activation import silu_and_mul
+    from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp4_utils import fp4_quantize
+
+    act = torch.empty(x.shape[0], x.shape[1] // 2, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+    silu_and_mul(x, act)
+    return fp4_quantize(act, global_scale)
+
+
+def fused(x, global_scale):
+    from flashinfer.quantization import silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quantize
+
+    return silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quantize(x, global_scale)
+
+
+def time_us(fn, mode):
+    if mode == "graph":
+        with torch.cuda.stream(torch.cuda.Stream()):
+            return triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(fn) * 1e3
+    return triton.testing.do_bench(fn) * 1e3
+
+
+def main():
+    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    p.add_argument("--tokens", type=int, nargs="+", default=TOKENS)
+    p.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, nargs="+", default=[0, 1, 2])
+    p.add_argument("--modes", nargs="+", default=["graph"])
+    p.add_argument("--json", help="also write every measurement to this file")
+    args = p.parse_args()
+
+    gpu = torch.cuda.get_device_name()
+    print(f"{gpu}, seeds {args.seeds}")
+    print(
+        f"{'mode':5s} {'model':14s} {'d':>6s} {'tokens':>7s} {'unfused us':>11s} "
+        f"{'fused us':>9s} {'speedup':>8s} {'std':>6s} {'mismatch':>9s}"
+    )
+    rows = []
+    for mode in args.modes:
+        for name, d in MODELS.items():
+            for m in args.tokens:
+                t_u, t_f, mismatch = [], [], 0.0
+                for seed in args.seeds:
+                    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+                    x = torch.randn(m, 2 * d, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") * 3
+                    amax = torch.empty(1).uniform_(10.0, 30.0).item()
+                    global_scale = torch.tensor([448.0 * 6.0 / amax], device="cuda")
+                    ref_fp4, _ = unfused(x, global_scale)
+                    fp4, _ = fused(x, global_scale)
+                    err = (ref_fp4.view(torch.uint8) != fp4).float().mean().item()
+                    assert err <= 2e-3, err
+                    mismatch = max(mismatch, err)
+                    t_u.append(time_us(lambda: unfused(x, global_scale), mode))
+                    t_f.append(time_us(lambda: fused(x, global_scale), mode))
+                speedups = [u / f for u, f in zip(t_u, t_f)]
+                sd = statistics.stdev(speedups) if len(speedups) > 1 else 0.0
+                print(
+                    f"{mode:5s} {name:14s} {d:6d} {m:7d} {statistics.mean(t_u):11.1f} "
+                    f"{statistics.mean(t_f):9.1f} {statistics.mean(speedups):7.2f}x "
+                    f"{sd:6.3f} {mismatch:9.1e}"
+                )
+                rows.append(
+                    dict(
+                        gpu=gpu,
+                        mode=mode,
+                        model=name,
+                        d=d,
+                        tokens=m,
+                        seeds=args.seeds,
+                        unfused_us=t_u,
+                        fused_us=t_f,
+                        speedup=speedups,
+                        mismatch=mismatch,
+                    )
+                )
+    if args.json:
+        with open(args.json, "w") as f:
+            json.dump(rows, f, indent=1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""SiluAndMul fused with the NVFP4 activation quant of the next linear (FlashInfer's kernel)
+gives the same FP4 codes and block scales as silu_and_mul followed by fp4_quantize."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.activation import SiluAndMul, silu_and_mul
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.schemes import (
+    CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4,
+)
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp4_utils import fp4_quantize
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, enter_scope, published_topology
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+
+def _sf_offsets(rows: int, groups: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Offsets of the [rows, groups] block scales in the 128x4 swizzled layout."""
+    k_tiles = (groups + 3) // 4
+    m = torch.arange(rows).unsqueeze(1)
+    k = torch.arange(groups).unsqueeze(0)
+    return (
+        (m // 128) * k_tiles * 512
+        + (k // 4) * 512
+        + (m % 32) * 16
+        + ((m % 128) // 32) * 4
+        + (k % 4)
+    ).cuda()
+
+
+@unittest.skipIf(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] < 10,
+    "NVFP4 activation quantization requires SM100+",
+)
+class TestSiluAndMulNvfp4Quant(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        enter_scope(self, published_topology())
+
+    def _fused_act(self, global_scale):
+        down_proj = SimpleNamespace(
+            scheme=CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4(), input_global_scale=global_scale
+        )
+        act = SiluAndMul()
+        act.fuse_output_quant(down_proj)
+        self.assertIs(act._quant_linear, down_proj)
+        return act
+
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_matches_silu_and_mul_then_fp4_quantize(self):
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        for tokens in (1, 37, 300, 4100):
+            for d in (1536, 4096, 14336):
+                with self.subTest(tokens=tokens, d=d):
+                    x = torch.randn(tokens, 2 * d, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+                    act_ref = torch.empty(tokens, d, dtype=x.dtype, device="cuda")
+                    silu_and_mul(x, act_ref)
+                    global_scale = (448.0 * 6.0 / act_ref.float().abs().amax()).reshape(
+                        1
+                    )
+                    ref_fp4, ref_sf = fp4_quantize(act_ref, global_scale)
+
+                    # The kernel itself, also below the fusion's token threshold.
+                    fp4, sf, dtype, leading = self._fused_act(
+                        global_scale
+                    )._forward_nvfp4_quant(x)
+
+                    self.assertEqual((dtype, leading), (torch.bfloat16, (tokens,)))
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        torch.equal(fp4.view(torch.uint8), ref_fp4.view(torch.uint8))
+                    )
+                    offsets = _sf_offsets(tokens, d // 16)
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        torch.equal(
+                            sf.view(torch.uint8).flatten()[offsets],
+                            ref_sf.view(torch.uint8).flatten()[offsets],
+                        )
+                    )
+
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_leading_dims_are_kept_for_the_linear(self):
+        x = torch.randn(2, 128, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        fp4, _, _, leading = self._fused_act(
+            torch.tensor([100.0], device="cuda")
+        ).forward_cuda(x)
+        self.assertEqual(leading, (2, 128))
+        self.assertEqual(fp4.shape, (256, 32))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+"""Which SiluAndMul outputs are fused with the NVFP4 activation quant of the next linear."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from sglang.srt.layers import activation
+from sglang.srt.layers.activation import SiluAndMul
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.compressed_tensors.schemes import (
+    CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, enter_scope, published_topology
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _linear(scheme=None):
+    linear = nn.Linear(4, 4)
+    if scheme is not None:
+        linear.scheme = scheme
+    return linear
+
+
+class TestFuseOutputQuant(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        enter_scope(self, published_topology())
+        enter_scope(self, patch.object(activation, "_is_cuda", True))
+        enter_scope(
+            self,
+            patch.object(
+                activation, "_flashinfer_silu_and_mul_nvfp4_available", lambda: True
+            ),
+        )
+
+    def test_other_devices_never_fuse(self):
+        act = SiluAndMul()
+        with patch.object(activation, "_is_cuda", False):
+            act.fuse_output_quant(_linear(CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4()))
+        self.assertIsNone(act._quant_linear)
+
+    def test_needs_the_flashinfer_kernel(self):
+        act = SiluAndMul()
+        with patch.object(
+            activation, "_flashinfer_silu_and_mul_nvfp4_available", lambda: False
+        ):
+            act.fuse_output_quant(_linear(CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4()))
+        self.assertIsNone(act._quant_linear)
+
+    def test_keeps_only_w4a4_nvfp4_linears(self):
+        nvfp4, plain, other_scheme = SiluAndMul(), SiluAndMul(), SiluAndMul()
+        down = _linear(CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4())
+        nvfp4.fuse_output_quant(down)
+        plain.fuse_output_quant(_linear())
+        other_scheme.fuse_output_quant(_linear(SimpleNamespace()))
+
+        self.assertIs(nvfp4._quant_linear, down)
+        self.assertIsNone(plain._quant_linear)
+        self.assertIsNone(other_scheme._quant_linear)
+
+    def test_projection_is_not_a_child_module(self):
+        act = SiluAndMul()
+        act.fuse_output_quant(_linear(CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4()))
+        self.assertEqual(list(act.children()), [])
+        self.assertEqual(list(act.parameters()), [])
+
+    def test_fusable_inputs(self):
+        bf16 = torch.empty(256, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        self.assertTrue(activation._can_fuse_nvfp4_act_quant(bf16))
+        self.assertTrue(activation._can_fuse_nvfp4_act_quant(bf16.to(torch.float16)))
+        self.assertFalse(activation._can_fuse_nvfp4_act_quant(bf16.float()))
+        strided = torch.empty(256, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16)[:, :64]
+        self.assertFalse(activation._can_fuse_nvfp4_act_quant(strided))
+        self.assertFalse(
+            activation._can_fuse_nvfp4_act_quant(
+                torch.empty(256, 48, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            )
+        )
+
+    def test_lora_and_sequence_parallelism_keep_the_unfused_path(self):
+        x = torch.empty(256, 64, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        with patch.object(
+            activation, "get_lora", return_value=SimpleNamespace(enable_lora=True)
+        ):
+            self.assertFalse(activation._can_fuse_nvfp4_act_quant(x))
+        with patch.object(
+            activation, "get_forward", return_value=SimpleNamespace(sp_active=True)
+        ):
+            self.assertFalse(activation._can_fuse_nvfp4_act_quant(x))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

**Issue**

`_accepts_nvfp4_input` uses `getattr(linear, "scheme", None)` and `getattr(scheme, "accepts_prequantized_input", False)`. SGLang does not allow defensive `getattr`. `LinearBase` already defines `scheme = None` for exactly this `is None` check. If the flag is renamed later, this code silently turns the fusion off instead of failing.

**Fix**

Type the argument as `LinearBase` and read the field directly: `isinstance(linear.scheme, CompressedTensorsW4A4Fp4)` with a local import. Or declare `accepts_prequantized_input: bool = False` on `BaseLinearScheme` and check `linear.scheme is not None and linear.scheme.accepts_prequantized_input`. The CPU test's `_linear()` helper then needs a real `scheme` field.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

This adds a second way for an NVFP4 linear to take a pre-quantized input. `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod.apply` already accepts an `(fp4, scale)` tuple when `layer._accepts_prequantized_fp4` is set (used by `qwen3_5.py` and `deepseek_v2.py`). This PR adds a scheme flag and a different 4-tuple, `(fp4, scale, dtype, leading_dims)`, for compressed-tensors only. So `SiluAndMul.fuse_output_quant` never fuses ModelOpt NVFP4 Llama/Qwen2/Qwen3 checkpoints, although their `down_proj` can already take a quantized input.

**Fix**

Use one opt-in and one tuple layout for both NVFP4 linear methods, and let `fuse_output_quant` accept ModelOpt W4A4 linears too. If ModelOpt is out of scope for this PR, say so in the description.
